item.title: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, an elder bhikkhu is loved, liked, respected, and an example for his fellow celibates. What five? He is virtuous, living…
item.description:
Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, an elder bhikkhu is loved, liked, respected, and an example for his fellow celibates. What five? He is virtuous, living restrained by the restraint of the Pātimokkha, perfect in conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, undertaking and training in the training rules; he is learned, remembers what he has learned, accumulates what he has learned. Those teachings that are beautiful in the beginning, beautiful in the middle, beautiful in the end, with meaning and phrasing, revealing the completely perfected and purified holy life — such teachings he has learned much, memorized, remembered by repeated recitation, investigated with the mind, and well penetrated by right view; he speaks well, uses fine speech, his words are refined, clear in meaning, his voice not faltering or hoarse, he explains the meaning clearly; he attains without difficulty, without trouble, without effort the four jhānas that are higher states of mind, pleasant abidings in this very life; by the destruction of the taints, he in this very life, with direct knowledge, realizes, attains, and abides in the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom.
Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, an elder bhikkhu is loved, liked, respected, and an example for his fellow celibates.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.87

item.title: Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu, those taints that are to be abandoned by seeing have been abandoned by seeing, those taints that are to be abandoned…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu, those taints that are to be abandoned by seeing have been abandoned by seeing, those taints that are to be abandoned by restraining have been abandoned by restraining ... That bhikkhu is called one who dwells restraining all taints, who has cut off craving, who has turned away from the fetters, who has fully broken through conceit, who has put an end to suffering.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 2 – Sabbāsavasutta

item.title: Bhikkhus, when the community of bhikkhus gathers in harmony, disperses in harmony, and carries out Saṅgha business in harmony, then, bhikkhus, the community of bhikkhus…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, when the community of bhikkhus gathers in harmony, disperses in harmony, and carries out Saṅgha business in harmony, then, bhikkhus, the community of bhikkhus will grow and not decline. Bhikkhus, when the community of bhikkhus does not decree what has not been decreed, does not abolish what has been decreed, and lives following the training rules as decreed, then, bhikkhus, the community of bhikkhus will grow and not decline. Bhikkhus, when the community of bhikkhus honors, respects, reveres, and makes offerings to the elder bhikkhus — those of long experience, long ordained, the fathers and leaders of the Saṅgha — and listens to their guidance, then, bhikkhus, the community of bhikkhus will grow and not decline.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.23

item.title: Elder Soṇa Koḷivisa: Formerly, high in the state, serving the king of Aṅga, Now high in the Dhamma, Soṇa has overcome suffering. Five are cut,…
item.description:
Elder Soṇa Koḷivisa:

Formerly, high in the state, serving the king of Aṅga,
Now high in the Dhamma, Soṇa has overcome suffering.

Five are cut, five abandoned, five higher qualities are developed.
A bhikkhu who has crossed five strands is called one who has crossed the flood.

A bhikkhu of arrogant nature, heedless, delighting in external tastes,
Does not perfect virtue, concentration, and wisdom.

What should be done is abandoned; what should not be done is done.
For the arrogant and heedless, the taints increase.

Those who are diligently, constantly developing mindfulness of the body,
Do not do what should not be done, persist in what should be done.
For the mindful and aware, the taints are destroyed.

The straight path is taught — walk on it, do not turn back.
Reproach yourself, bring Nibbāna near.

When I was striving with overstrained energy,
The Unsurpassed Teacher of the world,
Using the simile of the lute, the One with the Dhamma-eye, the Seer,
Taught me the Dhamma.

I heard his teaching and dwelled happily in that instruction.
Calm, I practiced to attain the supreme goal.
I have attained the three knowledges; done is the Buddha's teaching.

One who is intent on renunciation, mind inclined to seclusion,
One who is intent on non-hatred, destroying all grasping,

One who is intent on the destruction of craving, mind without delusion,
Seeing the arising of the base, the mind is well liberated.

A bhikkhu whose mind is pure, rightly liberated,
Has nothing stored up, nothing left to do.

Like a solid rock, not shaken by the wind,
So too, regarding all forms, tastes, sounds, scents, touches,

Pleasant and unpleasant phenomena — unshaken,
That one's mind is established, unattached,
Contemplating their destruction.

From: Theragāthā 13.1

item.title: Do not ask about birth, ask about conduct. Indeed, from any wood a fire is born. From a lowly family, a sage of wisdom, Well-trained,…
item.description:
Do not ask about birth, ask about conduct.
Indeed, from any wood a fire is born.
From a lowly family, a sage of wisdom,
Well-trained, restrained by moral shame,

Trained in truth, subdued and controlled,
One who has attained knowledge, fulfilled the holy life —
At the proper time offer him offerings.
Therefore, any brahmin seeking merit
Should perform the sacrifice with such offerings.

From: Sutta Nipāta 3.4

item.title: - Venerable Sir, the Blessed One does not enable me to attain the superhuman states of psychic power. - Sunakkhatta, did I say to you:…
item.description:
- Venerable Sir, the Blessed One does not enable me to attain the superhuman states of psychic power. - Sunakkhatta, did I say to you: 'Come, Sunakkhatta, live under my guidance! I will enable you to attain the superhuman states of psychic power'? - No, Venerable Sir. - Did you say to me: 'Venerable Sir, I will live under the guidance of the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will enable me to attain the superhuman states of psychic power'? - No, Venerable Sir. - Sunakkhatta, since I did not say to you, and you did not say to me, you foolish man, who are you and who am I that you speak of abandoning? Sunakkhatta, whether the superhuman states of psychic power are realized or not, the purpose for which I teach the Dhamma is to lead the practitioner to the complete destruction of suffering. Sunakkhatta, what then are the superhuman states of psychic power that need to be realized? See how great your transgression is, you foolish man!

From: Dīgha Nikāya 24 – Pāthikasutta

item.title: There is no entering upon the unwholesome, bhikkhus, as long as moral shame... moral dread... energy... wisdom are established in wholesome states. When moral shame...…
item.description:
There is no entering upon the unwholesome, bhikkhus, as long as moral shame... moral dread... energy... wisdom are established in wholesome states. When moral shame... moral dread... energy... wisdom disappear, bhikkhus, then shamelessness... fearlessness... laziness... evil wisdom arise and persist, then there is entering upon the unwholesome.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.6

item.title: Nigrodha, you are wise and senior, have you ever thought: 'The Buddha, the Enlightened One, teaches the Dhamma that leads to enlightenment; the Blessed One,…
item.description:
Nigrodha, you are wise and senior, have you ever thought: 'The Buddha, the Enlightened One, teaches the Dhamma that leads to enlightenment; the Blessed One, the Tamed One, teaches the Dhamma that leads to taming; the Blessed One, the Calmed One, teaches the Dhamma that leads to calming; the Blessed One, the One Gone to the Far Shore, teaches the Dhamma that leads to the far shore; the Blessed One, the One of Perfect Peace, teaches the Dhamma that leads to perfect peace.'

From: Dīgha Nikāya 25 – Udumbarika­sīhanādasutta

item.title: Ānanda, I have declared unequivocally that evil bodily action, evil verbal action, and evil mental action should not be done. If one does what should…
item.description:
Ānanda, I have declared unequivocally that evil bodily action, evil verbal action, and evil mental action should not be done. If one does what should not be done, the following dangers are to be expected: self-reproach; after being known, the wise reproach; a bad reputation spreads; one dies confused; and after death, with the breakup of the body, one is reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Therefore, Ānanda, I have declared unequivocally that evil bodily action, evil verbal action, and evil mental action should not be done. For one who does what should not be done, these are the dangers to be expected.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 2.18

item.title: Associate with a learned friend who upholds the Dhamma, A great-hearted, intelligent, and eloquent companion. Knowing the meaning, dispelling doubts, Live alone like a rhinoceros.…
item.description:
Associate with a learned friend who upholds the Dhamma,
A great-hearted, intelligent, and eloquent companion.
Knowing the meaning, dispelling doubts,
Live alone like a rhinoceros.

Not delighting in the pleasures of the world — song, dance, and sensual pleasures —
Wandering without adornment, without longing,
Uttering the truth, rejecting all ornament,
Live alone like a rhinoceros.

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.3
